meta.title: Orange County Food Assistance
meta.subtitle: County-Wide Food Assistance Directory
meta.disclaimer: Information is subject to change due to increases in utilization. Please call the location before you go to confirm availability, hours, and documentation requirements. Most pantries ask for ID, proof of address, and that you bring your own bags.

programs.name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)
programs.description: Household must meet certain income and resource limits, and work requirements to be eligible to receive SNAP benefits. Although not typically eligible for SNAP, students and non-citizens can receive SNAP benefits under specific qualifications. Non-citizens generally must have lived in the U.S. for at least 5 years, be receiving disability-related assistance or benefits, or be children under 18. People experiencing homelessness do not need to meet certain residential requirements. Special rules apply for the elderly or disabled.
programs.howToEnroll: Apply via myBenefits (https://mybenefits.ny.gov/mybenefits/begin), call Orange County Department of Social Services at 845-291-2002, call United Way 211, or contact Cornerstone Family Healthcare Enabling Services at 845-926-3636 / Jduran@cornerstonefh.org.

programs.name: Women, Infants, and Children Program (WIC)
programs.description: Applicants must meet all eligibility requirements: Categorical (pregnant women during pregnancy and up to 6 weeks after birth/end of pregnancy; postpartum up to six months after birth; breastfeeding up to infant's first birthday; infants up to first birthday; children up to fifth birthday); Residential (must live in the state of application); Income (at or below state income standard, or automatically income-eligible via SNAP, Medicaid, TANF, etc.); Nutrition Risk (determined by health professional or WIC staff). Non-citizens are eligible if they meet general eligibility requirements.
programs.howToEnroll: Contact a local WIC clinic (Cornerstone Family Healthcare or Sun River Health) to apply. Must meet categorical, residential, income, and nutrition-risk requirements.

programs.name: Home Delivered Meal Program
programs.description: Nutritious noontime meals are distributed to elderly residents in many locations in Orange County, with nutrition education and counseling with a registered dietician provided as needed. Arrangements may be made for weekend service and limited diet modifications. A pre-screening process is required; final approval depends on an in-home assessment. Food delivery once a week after sign-up. Serves all Orange County residents except Village of Warwick.

programs.schedule: Food delivery once a week after sign-up; weekend service may be arranged
programs.howToEnroll: Call Orange County NY Connects at 845-615-3710 to complete a referral for Home Delivered Meals. Pre-screening required; final approval dependent upon in-home assessment.

programs.name: Meals on Wheels – Newburgh and New Windsor
programs.description: Any individual residing in Newburgh or New Windsor who is home-bound and has difficulty cooking—because of age, illness, injury or disability—can apply to receive meals. There is a modest charge for those who are able to pay; participates in most managed long-term care insurance plans; relies on donations to cover remaining costs.
programs.howToEnroll: Apply at https://www.mealsonwheelsnewburgh.org/how-apply or call 845-562-3490.

programs.name: Meals on Wheels – Town/Village of Warwick
programs.description: Meals provided to homebound and/or elderly individuals who are unable to shop or cook for themselves due to age, illness or disability. Fresh meals prepared daily at Mt. Alverno Center. Hot meals (meat, starch, vegetables, milk or juice, bread and butter, dessert or fruit) and cold meals (sandwich, salad, milk or juice, dessert) available; customized to dietary needs. Modest charge for meals. Deliveries to Village of Warwick and some surrounding areas in the Town of Warwick.
programs.howToEnroll: Call Meals on Wheels of Warwick at 845-986-3389 and leave a voicemail. A representative will contact you. Meal delivery starts soon after enrollment. Also apply at https://www.mealsonwheelsofwarwickny.org/apply-for-meals.

programs.name: Summer EBT Food Benefits for New York State
programs.description: The Summer Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) program helps families buy food for their school-aged children during the summer. Families get $120 in food benefits for each eligible child on an EBT card, usable for fruits, vegetables, meat, whole grains, and dairy at authorized retail food stores, farmers' markets, and anywhere SNAP is accepted. Unused benefits expire and are removed 122 days from issuance. Apply before September 8, 2026 deadline for 2026 benefits if no OTDA communication received by mid-June.
programs.howToEnroll: Visit otda.ny.gov/SummerEBT to learn when and how benefits are issued and how to use them. If no communications from NYS OTDA by mid-June, apply before the September 8, 2026 deadline for 2026 benefits.
